title: Sauna Protocol: Bryan's daily dry sauna routine and how to copy it at home
summary: Bryan ran a 30-day dry sauna experiment and calls sauna one of the most efficacious longevity protocols he has done. He shares his own protocol (200°F, 20 min, daily), a home version (80-100°C, 15-20 min, 3-5x/week), his toxin, microplastic, vascular and fertility results, and safety cautions.

principles.text: Dry sauna is a high-value longevity protocol: 15-20 min, 3-7x a week, at 176-212°F (80-100°C).
principles.quote: dry sauna is great for longevity - do 15-20 min, 3-7x a week, 176-212°F (80-100°C)

principles.text: Bryan saunas daily at 200°F for 20 min in the morning after his workout.
principles.quote: Type: Dry sauna Temperature: 200°F (93°C) Relative air humidity: very low, 5-20% Duration: 20 min Frequency: Daily When: In the morning after my workout

principles.text: Long-term frequent sauna use is linked to markedly lower all-cause mortality.
principles.quote: Using a dry sauna 4+ times per week is linked to about a 40% lower risk of dying from any cause, compared to not using a sauna, based on long-term studies.

principles.text: Men should ice the testicles during sauna; without ice his fertility markers dropped sharply.
principles.quote: Most importantly for men, ice the boys. Icing the testicles prevents heat from damaging fertility markers.

principles.text: Beginners should aim for the lower end of the temperature range; very high heat causes side effects.
principles.quote: Aim for the lower end of this spectrum, especially as a beginner. Higher temperatures closer to the boiling point can cause side effects like headaches and severely dried nose and eyes.

principles.text: Never sauna dehydrated; rehydrate with water plus electrolytes afterward and shower to wash off toxins.
principles.quote: Never use a sauna when dehydrated, and drink plenty of water afterwards to rehydrate. In general, you might need to rehydrate with up to 16-32 oz (0.5-1 L) of fluid after a sauna session.
